## Emp

### `al-emp-006` — Highlight Sweep

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.5s sweep*

Highlights a key word like a marker pen.

**How:** A solid accent-colored box grows behind the word from 0% to 100% width over 0.5s (from the reading-start side: right for Arabic). The word color switches to dark for contrast. The box shrinks back on exit.

**Use when:** Highlights a key word like a marker pen.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-emp-007` — Underline Draw

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.6s draw*

A quiet emphasis on one word.

**How:** A rounded accent line (about 8% of the font size thick) draws under the word from the reading-start side to the end over 0.6s, holds, then retracts toward the far side.

**Use when:** A quiet emphasis on one word.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-emp-008` — Scale Punch

*workhorse · high · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.15s punch · 0.25s settle*

A strong word that needs a hit on the beat or a sound effect.

**How:** On the exact spoken frame the word jumps to 150% scale in 0.15s and turns accent color, then settles to 125% over 0.25s and holds. Return to 100% at the end. Pair it with a short "boom" or "pop" sound effect.

**Use when:** A strong word that needs a hit on the beat or a sound effect.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-emp-009` — Word Shake

*workhorse · calm · depth · evidence 0 · 0.6s shake*

Surprise, anger or a warning.

**How:** The word shakes horizontally with ±6% offsets and ±4° rotation, alternating every 0.04–0.05s for about 0.6s, with the amplitude damping toward zero.

**Use when:** Surprise, anger or a warning.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-emp-010` — Glitch Text

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.6s glitch burst*

Tech, AI and hacking topics.

**How:** For about 0.6s, two copies of the text (cyan #3FE0FF and red #FF3F6C) jitter ±5% offset and show through random horizontal slice masks, changing every 2–3 frames, while the main text skews ±8°. Then everything snaps back clean.

**Use when:** Tech, AI and hacking topics.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-emp-061` — Circle Around

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.6s draw*

Circles a key word as if drawn with a pen.

**How:** A hand-drawn accent ellipse strokes around the word over 0.6s (animated stroke), holds, then erases. Slightly uneven so it feels hand-made.

**Use when:** Circles a key word as if drawn with a pen.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-emp-062` — Strike Through

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.5s*

Crosses out a wrong or old word before the right one.

**How:** An accent line draws through the middle of the word from the reading-start side over 0.5s, holds, then retracts.

**Use when:** Crosses out a wrong or old word before the right one.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

Frames a word inside a drawn box.

**Use when:** Frames a word inside a drawn box.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

*workhorse · any · blur · evidence 0 · 0.15s*

A quick white flash on a strong word or cut.

**How:** A full-screen white flash rises to 90% opacity in 1–2 frames and fades out over 0.15s, exactly on the beat or word.

**Use when:** A quick white flash on a strong word or cut.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-emp-077` — Sparkle Stars

*workhorse · calm · depth · evidence 0 · loop · 1.2s*

Sparkles around a word or product for a "fresh" feel.

**How:** Three to five small four-point stars pop in around the word at random spots, scale 0 to 100% while rotating 90°, then shrink away, staggered by 0.3s.

**Use when:** Sparkles around a word or product for a "fresh" feel.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-emp-078` — Swing

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 1s*

A hanging word swings like a sign.

**How:** The word swings from its top edge: +16°, -11°, +7°, -4°, +2° and settles over about 1s.

**Use when:** A hanging word swings like a sign.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-emp-079` — Tilt Pop

*workhorse · high · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.3s*

A word grows with a small tilt, sticker style.

**How:** The word scales to 130% while rotating -8° in 0.3s, settles at 120% and -5°, holds, then returns.

**Use when:** A word grows with a small tilt, sticker style.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-emp-080` — Chromatic Split

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.5s*

A word splits into red and cyan channels, tech style.

**How:** Red and cyan copies of the word slide out sideways by 1.5% of the width and back in over 0.5s, like an RGB lens split.

**Use when:** A word splits into red and cyan channels, tech style.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

## Cap

### `al-cap-011` — Karaoke Highlight

*workhorse · any · blur · evidence 0 · synced to each word*

The main Reels caption: each word lights up as it is spoken.

**How:** A full caption line is shown in dimmed white (50% opacity). Each word turns accent color exactly at its spoken timestamp (word-level ASR timings) and stays colored. Bold display font about 64px at 1080 wide, centered, inside the safe zone (y 1350–1550).

**Use when:** The main Reels caption: each word lights up as it is spoken.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cap-012` — Word Pop

*workhorse · high · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.18s per word*

A fast, lively caption, word by word.

**How:** Each word appears at its spoken timestamp, scaling from 30% to 118% and settling to 100% in 0.18s. Earlier words stay. Clear the line when the sentence ends.

**Use when:** A fast, lively caption, word by word.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cap-013` — Bounce Caption

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.55s in*

A whole line drops in at once with a playful move.

**How:** The whole caption line enters from 130% below with a spring: overshoot to -14%, rebound to +6%, settle at 0 over about 0.55s. Fade out on exit.

**Use when:** A whole line drops in at once with a playful move.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cap-014` — Boxed Word

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · synced to each word*

TikTok-style caption where the box follows your voice.

**How:** A rounded accent box sits behind the currently spoken word only, and the word turns dark. When the next word starts, the box jumps to it, with a 6% scale pop. Other words stay white.

**Use when:** TikTok-style caption where the box follows your voice.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cap-015` — One-Word Caption

*workhorse · high · depth · evidence 0 · one word at a time*

Fast, punchy talk: one big word in the middle.

**How:** Only the current word is on screen, large (about 110px), centered. Each new word replaces the previous one with a quick scale from 60% to 110% to 100% over 0.15s. Optionally color key words in the accent.

**Use when:** Fast, punchy talk: one big word in the middle.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cap-081` — Two-Line Caption

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 0.45s per line · 0.4s stagger*

A long sentence split into two lines that appear in turn.

**How:** Split the sentence into two balanced lines. Each line rises 40px and fades in over 0.45s, the second starting 0.4s after the first. Keep both inside the safe zone.

**Use when:** A long sentence split into two lines that appear in turn.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cap-082` — Typewriter Caption

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · synced to speech*

A caption that types itself out with your voice.

**How:** The caption reveals character by character from the reading-start side, paced so it finishes when the sentence ends. No caret.

**Use when:** A caption that types itself out with your voice.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cap-083` — Fade Words

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.25s per word*

A calm caption, each word fades in.

**How:** Each word fades from 0 to 100% opacity over 0.25s at its spoken timestamp. Earlier words stay. Clear the line at the end of the sentence.

**Use when:** A calm caption, each word fades in.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cap-084` — Slide-Up Words

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.25s per word*

A lively caption, each word slides up.

**How:** Each word slides up from 60% below its line while fading in over 0.25s at its spoken timestamp.

**Use when:** A lively caption, each word slides up.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cap-085` — Underline Active Word

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · synced to each word*

A full caption with an underline that follows the spoken word.

**How:** The whole line is visible in white. A rounded accent bar sits under the word being spoken and jumps to the next word at its timestamp.

**Use when:** A full caption with an underline that follows the spoken word.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cap-086` — Scale Active Word

*workhorse · high · timeline · evidence 0 · synced to each word*

The spoken word grows and turns accent.

**How:** The word being spoken scales to 125% and turns the accent color; it returns to normal when the next word starts.

**Use when:** The spoken word grows and turns accent.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cap-087` — Color Sweep Line

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · sentence length*

A color fill sweeps along the whole line as you speak.

**How:** A two-color gradient is clipped to the caption text and slides from the reading-start side to the end over the sentence duration, so spoken parts turn accent.

**Use when:** A color fill sweeps along the whole line as you speak.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cap-088` — Keyword Color

*workhorse · high · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.2s*

A plain caption where only the key word lights up.

**How:** The caption stays white. Only the key word turns accent and scales to 112% at its timestamp, and stays like that until the line clears.

**Use when:** A plain caption where only the key word lights up.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cap-089` — Pill Caption

*workhorse · high · blur · evidence 0 · 0.3s in*

A caption inside a dark pill, readable on any footage.

**How:** The caption sits inside a dark rounded pill (85% opacity, generous padding). The pill pops from 60% to 105% to 100% over 0.3s.

**Use when:** A caption inside a dark pill, readable on any footage.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cap-090` — Outline Caption

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.45s in*

White caption with a thick black outline, classic and clear.

**How:** White bold caption with a black outline about 7% of the font size (stroke painted under the fill), no shadow. Enters with a fade-up.

**Use when:** White caption with a thick black outline, classic and clear.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cap-091` — Shadow Pop

*workhorse · high · depth · evidence 0 · 0.3s*

A caption with a solid colored drop shadow that pops, pop-art style.

**How:** A solid accent shadow (no blur) grows to 1.2% offset down-right while the text moves 1% up-left, so it looks lifted. Reverse at exit.

**Use when:** A caption with a solid colored drop shadow that pops, pop-art style.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

A soft cinematic caption, words resolve from blur.

**How:** Each word goes from 2% blur and opacity 0 to sharp and visible over 0.3s at its spoken timestamp.

**Use when:** A soft cinematic caption, words resolve from blur.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

Each word drops from above with a small bounce.

### `al-cap-098` — Bottom Bar Caption

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.4s bar · 0.3s text*

A caption inside a wide bottom bar, like the news.

**How:** A dark full-width bar grows from the right edge (0.4s), then the caption fades in inside it (0.3s). Text and bar retract at the end.

**Use when:** A caption inside a wide bottom bar, like the news.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cap-099` — Glitch Caption

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.4s glitch*

A tech caption that glitches as it lands.

**How:** The caption enters with a 0.4s glitch burst: red and cyan copies jitter through random slice masks, then the line snaps clean (see M-010).

**Use when:** A tech caption that glitches as it lands.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cap-100` — Progress Caption

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · sentence length*

A caption with a thin progress bar filling for the sentence.

**How:** Under the caption, a thin rounded accent bar fills from the reading-start side across the sentence duration, showing how long the line lasts.

**Use when:** A caption with a thin progress bar filling for the sentence.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cap-272` — Bilingual Caption

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · synced*

Arabic on top and English below, for a wider audience.

**How:** Show the Arabic caption in the main style and its English translation under it in a smaller lighter line; both enter together.

**Use when:** Arabic on top and English below, for a wider audience.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cap-273` — Text on Path

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · loop*

Text flowing along a curved path.

**How:** Lay the caption along a curved SVG path and slide its start offset so the words travel along the curve.

**Use when:** Text flowing along a curved path.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cap-274` — Full-Screen Kinetic

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · per word*

Huge words that swap and fill the whole screen.

**How:** Each word fills most of the frame in a bold display font and replaces the previous one on its timestamp, alternating background and text colors.

**Use when:** Huge words that swap and fill the whole screen.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cap-275` — Tagged Caption

*workhorse · high · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.3s*

The first word sits in a colored tag, the rest plain.

**How:** The caption pops in (M-089) with its first word inside a small accent box, like a label, followed by the rest of the line.

**Use when:** The first word sits in a colored tag, the rest plain.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cap-011-fast` — Karaoke Highlight · Fast

*accent · any · blur · evidence 0 · synced to each word*

Variant of M-011: أسرع بـ 40%

**Avoid when:** Same constraints as the base motion.

## Trn

### `al-trn-016` — Circle Reveal

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.6s*

Swap the background or scene from a point, like your finger or face.

**How:** The new scene is revealed through a circular mask that grows from a chosen point (e.g. a fingertip) from radius 0 to full-frame diagonal over 0.6s, with a 30px soft edge. A thin accent ring expands just ahead of the edge and fades out.

**Use when:** Swap the background or scene from a point, like your finger or face.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-trn-017` — Linear Wipe

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.5s*

A clear transition between two clips or places.

**How:** The new scene wipes in across the frame behind a moving vertical edge over 0.5s. The edge has a white 4px line with an accent glow.

**Use when:** A clear transition between two clips or places.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-trn-018` — Light Sweep

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.7s*

A magic change, like "look how it changed".

**How:** A bright warm diagonal light band (about 15% of the frame wide, angled 105°) sweeps across the frame over 0.7s. The scene swaps to the new one exactly as the band passes the center.

**Use when:** A magic change, like "look how it changed".

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-trn-019` — Zoom Blur

*workhorse · any · blur · evidence 0 · 0.4s out · 0.4s in*

A fast, punchy cut between two clips.

**How:** The outgoing clip scales to 170% with a radial blur of about 10px and fades out over 0.4s (easeInExpo). The incoming clip starts at 160% blurred and settles to 100% sharp over 0.4s (easeOutExpo).

**Use when:** A fast, punchy cut between two clips.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-trn-020` — Whip Pan

*workhorse · any · blur · evidence 0 · 0.35s*

Cut between two shots as if the camera spun.

**How:** The outgoing clip slides out to one side with heavy horizontal motion blur, and the incoming clip slides in from the opposite side over 0.35s total. Add a fast "whoosh" sound.

**Use when:** Cut between two shots as if the camera spun.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-trn-101` — Fade Through Black

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.3s out · 0.3s in*

A calm transition through a moment of black.

**How:** The outgoing clip fades to full black over 0.3s, holds black for 2–4 frames, then the new clip fades in from black over 0.3s.

**Use when:** A calm transition through a moment of black.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-trn-102` — Cross Dissolve

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.5s*

The classic soft blend from one shot into the next.

**How:** The new clip fades in on top of the old one from 0 to 100% over 0.5s while both play.

**Use when:** The classic soft blend from one shot into the next.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-trn-103` — Slide Push

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.45s*

The new shot pushes the old one off screen.

**How:** The new clip slides in from the right edge while pushing the old clip out to the left at the same speed over 0.45s.

**Use when:** The new shot pushes the old one off screen.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-trn-104` — Diagonal Wipe

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 0.5s*

A slanted wipe, livelier than a straight one.

**How:** The new clip is revealed behind a soft-edged diagonal line (135°) that travels from the top-left corner to the bottom-right over 0.5s.

**Use when:** A slanted wipe, livelier than a straight one.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-trn-105` — Iris Close/Open

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.4s close · 0.4s open*

A circle closes on one shot and opens on the next, old-film style.

**How:** A circular mask shrinks to zero on the face of the outgoing clip (0.4s), then the new clip opens from the same point with a growing circle (0.4s). Black between.

**Use when:** A circle closes on one shot and opens on the next, old-film style.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-trn-106` — Clock Wipe

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.6s*

The new shot sweeps in like a clock hand.

**How:** The new clip is revealed by a radial sweep around the center, starting at 12 o clock and going clockwise a full 360° over 0.6s.

**Use when:** The new shot sweeps in like a clock hand.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-trn-107` — Blinds

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.5s*

The new shot opens through vertical blinds.

**How:** The frame is split into 6 vertical strips. Each strip reveals the new clip by growing from its right edge to full width over 0.5s.

**Use when:** The new shot opens through vertical blinds.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-trn-108` — Split Doors

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.6s*

The shot splits in half and opens like doors.

**How:** The outgoing clip is cut down the middle; the two halves slide apart to the left and right over 0.6s, revealing the new clip behind them.

**Use when:** The shot splits in half and opens like doors.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-trn-109` — Diamond Reveal

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.6s*

The new shot opens from a growing diamond.

**How:** The new clip is revealed through a diamond-shaped mask that grows from the face point until it covers the frame over 0.6s.

**Use when:** The new shot opens from a growing diamond.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-trn-110` — Glitch Transition

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.4s*

A glitchy cut, great for cyber content.

**How:** For 0.4s the new clip flashes in through random horizontal slices with ±8% offsets, changing every 2 frames, then locks in clean. Add a digital noise sound.

**Use when:** A glitchy cut, great for cyber content.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-trn-111` — Spin Transition

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 0.5s*

The old shot spins out, the new one spins in.

**How:** The outgoing clip rotates 180° while shrinking to 20% and fading out; the new clip rotates in from -180° and 20% to full size over 0.5s.

**Use when:** The old shot spins out, the new one spins in.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

A cut hidden in a white flash, bold and sudden.

## Cam

### `al-cam-021` — Punch-In

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · instant (1 frame)*

Hides cuts between lines, or stresses a line.

**How:** The frame jumps instantly from 100% to 125% scale, centered on the face, on a cut or a key word. Hold, then jump back to 100% on the next cut. No easing.

**Use when:** Hides cuts between lines, or stresses a line.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-022` — Slow Push-In

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · whole shot (3–6s)*

A serious moment or a story.

**How:** The frame scales smoothly from 100% to about 116% across the whole shot, centered slightly above the face.

**Use when:** A serious moment or a story.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-023` — Camera Shake

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 0.3–1s*

With a hit, an explosion or a strong word.

**How:** Overscale the frame to 108% to hide the edges, then shift it with random ±1.5% offsets and ±0.8° rotation, changing every 2–3 frames. Damp the shake toward the end.

**Use when:** With a hit, an explosion or a strong word.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-024` — Zoom-Out Card

*workhorse · high · depth · evidence 0 · 0.6s out · 0.5s back*

Like "zoom out", or to show something next to the video.

**How:** The whole video shrinks to 60% scale with -3° tilt, about 48px rounded corners and a deep drop shadow over a dark patterned backdrop (0.6s). Hold, then it returns to full frame with a small 104% overshoot (0.5s).

**Use when:** Like "zoom out", or to show something next to the video.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-025` — Ken Burns

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · whole shot (4–8s)*

Bring a still photo to life.

**How:** A still image slowly scales from 112% to 132% while panning diagonally by about 10% of the frame across the whole duration.

**Use when:** Bring a still photo to life.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-121` — Dolly Zoom

*workhorse · calm · depth · evidence 0 · 1–2s*

The background stretches while you stay put, a shock or realization.

**How:** Using the person matte, scale the background layer from 100% to about 150% while scaling the person layer from 100% to about 86% from the bottom center, so the subject seems fixed while the room warps.

**Use when:** The background stretches while you stay put, a shock or realization.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-122` — Pan

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · 2–4s*

Moves the frame left and right across a shot or photo.

**How:** Overscale the frame to 125% and move it horizontally from +8% to -8% of the width across the shot.

**Use when:** Moves the frame left and right across a shot or photo.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-123` — Tilt Up

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · 2–4s*

The frame moves bottom to top, like revealing a person or building.

**How:** Overscale the frame to 125% and move it vertically from +9% to -7% of the height across the shot.

**Use when:** The frame moves bottom to top, like revealing a person or building.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-124` — Rack Focus

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 0.6s*

Focus shifts between the person and the background.

**How:** Using the person matte, blur the background from 0 to about 1.2% while the person goes from 1.2% blur to sharp over 0.6s, or the reverse.

**Use when:** Focus shifts between the person and the background.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-125` — Whip Zoom

*workhorse · any · blur · evidence 0 · 0.25s*

A quick zoom with motion blur onto the face.

**How:** Scale the frame to 150% with about 1.2% motion blur in 0.15s, then settle to 130% and sharp over 0.2s. Pair with a short whoosh.

**Use when:** A quick zoom with motion blur onto the face.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-126` — Handheld Drift

*workhorse · calm · depth · evidence 0 · loop · 4s*

Makes a locked-off shot feel handheld.

**How:** Overscale to 108% and drift the frame slowly with small offsets (±1.2%) and rotation (±0.5°) on a smooth 4s path.

**Use when:** Makes a locked-off shot feel handheld.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-127` — Dutch Tilt

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 0.5s*

Tilting the frame adds tension or unease.

**How:** Rotate the frame to -9° while scaling to 120% to hide the corners over 0.5s, hold, then return.

**Use when:** Tilting the frame adds tension or unease.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-128` — Snap Zoom Out

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.2s*

Starts close then snaps wide to show the whole scene.

**How:** Start at 150% on a detail, then snap out to 100% in about 0.2s on a beat or word.

**Use when:** Starts close then snaps wide to show the whole scene.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-129` — Crash Zoom

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.2s + 0.3s shake*

A hard zoom onto the face with a shake, for surprise.

**How:** Snap the frame to about 190% centered on the face in 0.15s, add a short horizontal shake (±1.5%), then hold. Pair with a dramatic hit.

**Use when:** A hard zoom onto the face with a shake, for surprise.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-130` — Orbit

*workhorse · calm · depth · evidence 0 · loop · 4s*

Feels like the camera is circling you slightly.

**How:** Apply a 3D Y-axis rotation of ±14° with perspective and a 112% scale, swinging smoothly every 4s.

**Use when:** Feels like the camera is circling you slightly.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-131` — Double Punch

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 2 cuts*

Two punch-ins in a row for strong emphasis.

**How:** Jump to 115% on the first beat and to 132% on the second, with no easing, then cut back to 100%.

**Use when:** Two punch-ins in a row for strong emphasis.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-132` — Split Screen

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.5s in*

Shows two shots side by side, like a comparison.

**How:** Two clips slide in from the left and right edges into each half of the frame over 0.5s, with a thin gap between them.

**Use when:** Shows two shots side by side, like a comparison.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-133` — Picture in Picture

*workhorse · high · depth · evidence 0 · 0.4s in*

A small video in the corner, like a reaction cam.

**How:** A rounded window with a white border and shadow (about 38% of the width) pops into the top corner from scale 0 over 0.4s and plays the second clip.

**Use when:** A small video in the corner, like a reaction cam.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-134` — Mirror Flip

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 0.5s*

The frame flips horizontally, like "the opposite is true".

**How:** Flip the frame horizontally (scaleX from 1 to -1) over 0.5s, hold, then flip back.

**Use when:** The frame flips horizontally, like "the opposite is true".

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-135` — Freeze Frame

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · hold 1–2s*

The shot freezes with muted color and a tag.

**How:** On the chosen frame, hold the image, desaturate it about 85% with a little more contrast, and pop a small label tag. Resume playback after the hold.

**Use when:** The shot freezes with muted color and a tag.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-136` — Slow Motion

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · ramp 0.2s*

An important moment slows down so viewers catch it.

**How:** Ramp the clip speed from 100% down to about 25% over 0.2s at the key moment (use frame blending or interpolation), hold, then ramp back.

**Use when:** An important moment slows down so viewers catch it.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-137` — Speed Ramp

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.8s*

Motion slows then speeds up suddenly, action style.

**How:** Combine a slow push (100% to 104%) with a sudden fast push to 130% in about 0.15s, then ease into a slow drift. Time the fast part to the beat.

**Use when:** Motion slows then speeds up suddenly, action style.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-138` — Letterbox Bars

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 0.5s in*

Black bars top and bottom for a film look.

**How:** Two black bars slide in from the top and bottom edges over 0.5s, each about 16% of the width tall, and stay during the cinematic part.

**Use when:** Black bars top and bottom for a film look.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-139` — Vignette Focus

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.6s in*

The edges darken so the eye goes to the face.

**How:** Fade in an elliptical dark vignette (transparent center, about 90% black at the edges) over 0.6s around the face.

**Use when:** The edges darken so the eye goes to the face.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-cam-140` — Bounce Zoom

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.5s*

A zoom that bounces a little before settling.

**How:** Zoom to 132%, bounce back to 116%, then 124%, and settle at 122% over about 0.5s.

**Use when:** A zoom that bounces a little before settling.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

## Fx

### `al-fx-026` — Particle Dissolve

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 1.2s*

A logo or object breaks apart and vanishes, like a finger snap.

**How:** The object breaks into 150–400 small particles sampled from its own pixels. Each particle flies outward on a random vector (60–250px) with slight upward drift, shrinks and fades out over 1.2s. The original disappears in the first 0.1s.

**Use when:** A logo or object breaks apart and vanishes, like a finger snap.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-027` — Shockwave

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 0.8s*

With a finger snap or a tap.

**How:** From the tap point, a white flash dot pops in and out (0.25s), then two accent rings expand from 0 to about 3.5x and fade, 0.12s apart. Optionally add a slight refraction on the video under the rings.

**Use when:** With a finger snap or a tap.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-028` — Pulse Rings

*workhorse · calm · depth · evidence 0 · loop · 1s per ring*

Behind your head when you talk about something important.

**How:** Concentric accent rings spawn behind the person (on the background layer, masked by the person matte) every 1/3 of the loop, expanding from 50% to 300% and fading to 0.

**Use when:** Behind your head when you talk about something important.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-029` — Light Rays

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · loop · 8s per turn*

A "wow" moment or a new announcement.

**How:** Soft accent-colored rays (conic gradient, 6° rays every 22°) rotate slowly behind the person. A radial mask fades them out at about 45% radius. Place them on the layer behind the person matte.

**Use when:** A "wow" moment or a new announcement.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-030` — Confetti Burst

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 1.5s*

A celebration, an achievement or a big number.

**How:** 40–80 small rectangles in 4 brand colors burst from a point with random velocity (mostly upward, ±60°), spin randomly, then fall with gravity and fade out over 1.5s.

**Use when:** A celebration, an achievement or a big number.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-141` — Sparkle Trail

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · 1s*

A glowing point travels and leaves a trail.

**How:** A bright warm point moves along a curved path; 10–20 copies follow it with 0.05s delays, each shrinking and fading, forming a sparkle trail.

**Use when:** A glowing point travels and leaves a trail.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-142` — Dust Burst

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 1s*

Dust puffs out when something lands.

**How:** From the impact point, 15–30 soft blurred puffs in sand tones spread out and slightly up, growing to 160% and fading over 1s.

**Use when:** Dust puffs out when something lands.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-143` — Lens Flare

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · 1.5s*

A sun flare drifts across the frame for warmth.

**How:** A bright warm core with a soft halo and 3 small colored ghost circles moves diagonally across the frame (screen blend) over about 1.5s.

**Use when:** A sun flare drifts across the frame for warmth.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-144` — Scan Line

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · 1.2s*

A light line scans the frame like a scanner, techy.

**How:** A bright mint horizontal line with a wide glow travels from the top to the bottom of the frame over 1.2s.

**Use when:** A light line scans the frame like a scanner, techy.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-145` — Code Rain

*workhorse · calm · depth · evidence 0 · loop*

Falling code characters, perfect for cyber topics.

**How:** Columns of mint monospace characters fall at different speeds behind the person (background layer), each column fading at its tail.

**Use when:** Falling code characters, perfect for cyber topics.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-146` — Hologram

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · loop*

The person looks like a futuristic hologram.

**How:** Tint the person cyan, add moving horizontal scanlines over them (screen blend) and a subtle opacity flicker every couple of seconds.

**Use when:** The person looks like a futuristic hologram.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-147` — Electric Arc

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.6s*

A flickering electric arc for energy moments.

**How:** A jagged light-blue zigzag line with a glow flickers on and off 2–3 times between two points; redraw the zigzag randomly each flicker.

**Use when:** A flickering electric arc for energy moments.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-148` — Heat Glow

*workhorse · calm · depth · evidence 0 · loop · 2s*

A warm pulsing aura behind the person.

**How:** A large orange radial glow sits behind the person (background layer) and pulses between 90% and 108% scale every 2s.

**Use when:** A warm pulsing aura behind the person.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-149` — Floating Particles

*workhorse · calm · depth · evidence 0 · loop*

Small light specks float upward for a calm mood.

**How:** Spawn 12–25 small warm glowing dots at random x positions near the bottom; each drifts upward with slight sideways drift over 3–5s and fades.

**Use when:** Small light specks float upward for a calm mood.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-150` — Radial Ripple

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · loop · 1.5s*

Rings spread from a point like touching water.

**How:** Thin mint rings spawn at a point every 0.5s, expanding from 30% to 450% and fading out.

**Use when:** Rings spread from a point like touching water.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-151` — Grid Floor

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · loop · 1s*

A moving 3D grid floor, retro-tech style.

**How:** Draw a mint line grid on a plane tilted 60° in perspective at the bottom of the frame, scrolling toward the viewer one cell per second.

**Use when:** A moving 3D grid floor, retro-tech style.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-152` — Spark Burst

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.5s*

Spark streaks shoot out from a point on a hit or idea.

**How:** Twelve thin warm streaks shoot radially outward from a point, stretching as they go and fading over 0.5s.

**Use when:** Spark streaks shoot out from a point on a hit or idea.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-153` — Orbit Dots

*workhorse · calm · depth · evidence 0 · loop · 3s*

Dots orbit around a logo or word.

**How:** Three accent dots travel around a dashed circle centered on the subject, evenly spaced, one full turn every 3s.

**Use when:** Dots orbit around a logo or word.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-154` — Glow Outline

*workhorse · calm · blur · evidence 0 · loop · 2s*

A glowing edge around the person makes them pop.

**How:** Using the person matte, add an accent outer glow (drop shadow on the matte edge) that pulses from 0 to about 2.5% blur every 2s.

**Use when:** A glowing edge around the person makes them pop.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-155` — VHS Glitch

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · loop*

Old videotape look for nostalgia.

**How:** Add short horizontal frame jumps (±3%), brief color shifts, and a soft bright noise band that rolls up the frame every couple of seconds.

**Use when:** Old videotape look for nostalgia.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-156` — Film Grain

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · loop*

Grain and light flicker for a film feel.

**How:** Overlay fine moving noise at about 35% opacity, jumping position every frame, plus a tiny brightness flicker (±10%).

**Use when:** Grain and light flicker for a film feel.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-157` — Shine Sweep

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.8s*

A shine passes over a word or logo like metal.

**How:** A narrow bright diagonal band clipped to the text or logo sweeps across it from one side to the other over 0.8s.

**Use when:** A shine passes over a word or logo like metal.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-158` — Bokeh Lights

*workhorse · calm · depth · evidence 0 · loop · 4s*

Soft out-of-focus light circles behind the person.

**How:** Place 6–10 blurred warm circles of different sizes on the background layer; each drifts a little and gently grows and fades on a 4s loop.

**Use when:** Soft out-of-focus light circles behind the person.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-159` — Speed Lines

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · loop · 0.4s*

Manga speed lines around the face for shock or hype.

**How:** Draw thin white radial lines around the subject with a clear center, jittering in angle and scale every few frames.

**Use when:** Manga speed lines around the face for shock or hype.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-fx-160` — Face Tracking Box

*workhorse · calm · camera · evidence 0 · loop*

A box that tracks the face with a score, AI style.

**How:** Detect the face and draw four mint corner brackets around it that follow it smoothly, with a small mono label above like "FACE 98%".

**Use when:** A box that tracks the face with a score, AI style.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

## Lgo

### `al-lgo-036` — Logo Float

*workhorse · calm · depth · evidence 0 · loop · 3s*

A logo floating gently behind you.

**How:** The logo hovers behind the person (background layer, under the person matte) with a gentle ±9% vertical bob on a 3s sine loop and a soft glow.

**Use when:** A logo floating gently behind you.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-lgo-037` — Logo Spin-In

*workhorse · high · depth · evidence 0 · 0.7s*

Opening or closing a video.

**How:** The logo spins in from -220° and scale 0 to 0° and 112%, then settles at 100% over 0.7s total. Exit: shrink to 0 with a 90° turn.

**Use when:** Opening or closing a video.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-lgo-038` — Title Card Drop

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 0.55s in*

The tool or topic name, like a "Claude Opus 5.5" card.

**How:** A dark rounded card with an accent border, an icon on one side and a two-line title (bold mono title plus an accent subtitle) drops from above the frame with a spring and about a 10% overshoot. Holds, then slides back up.

**Use when:** The tool or topic name, like a "Claude Opus 5.5" card.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-lgo-039` — Lower Third

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.4s bar · 0.3s text*

Introduce your name or handle.

**How:** An accent bar grows in from the right edge (0.4s), then the name and the subtitle slide in 12% and fade in inside it (0.3s, 0.08s stagger). Holds, then the text fades and the bar retracts.

**Use when:** Introduce your name or handle.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-lgo-040` — Number Counter

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 1.2s count*

A stat or big number counting up.

**How:** A number counts up from 0 to the target value over 1.2s (easeOutExpo, fast at first, then slowing), in tabular monospaced digits with an accent color, and a label beneath. Optionally scale-punch the final value (M-008).

**Use when:** A stat or big number counting up.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-lgo-181` — Logo Mask Reveal

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.6s*

A logo rises from behind an invisible line, premium style.

**How:** The logo sits inside a box with hidden overflow and slides up from below its edge into place over 0.6s (see M-004).

**Use when:** A logo rises from behind an invisible line, premium style.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-lgo-182` — Logo Stroke Draw

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 1s draw · 0.4s fill*

The logo draws its outline, then fills.

**How:** Animate the logo vector outline stroke from 0 to full length over 1s, then fade in the fill over 0.4s.

**Use when:** The logo draws its outline, then fills.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-lgo-183` — Logo Glitch

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.4s burst*

The logo glitches with split colors, techy.

**How:** For about 0.4s the logo jumps a few percent in random directions with red and cyan offset copies, then snaps back clean.

**Use when:** The logo glitches with split colors, techy.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-lgo-184` — Logo Bounce

*workhorse · high · depth · evidence 0 · 0.8s*

The logo drops in and bounces twice.

**How:** The logo falls from above the frame, lands, bounces up 30% then 10% and settles over about 0.8s.

**Use when:** The logo drops in and bounces twice.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-lgo-185` — Logo Shine

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.8s*

A shine passes over a logo badge.

**How:** A bright diagonal band sweeps across the logo badge from one side to the other over 0.8s, clipped to the badge shape.

**Use when:** A shine passes over a logo badge.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-lgo-186` — Logo Assemble

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 1s*

Particles gather into the logo, the reverse of M-026.

**How:** Hundreds of particles start scattered and fly inward to their positions in the logo over 1s; when they arrive, the solid logo fades in and the particles disappear.

**Use when:** Particles gather into the logo, the reverse of M-026.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-lgo-187` — End Card

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 0.6s in*

The closing card: logo, handle and a follow prompt.

**How:** The logo scales in, then the handle and a "تابعني" line fade up under it 0.15s apart. Hold until the end of the video.

**Use when:** The closing card: logo, handle and a follow prompt.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-lgo-188` — Watermark Corner

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 0.6s in*

Your logo small in the corner for the whole video.

**How:** The logo flies from the center to a top corner while shrinking, then stays there at about 55% opacity and 12% of the width for the rest of the video.

**Use when:** Your logo small in the corner for the whole video.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.3s*

A stamp hits the screen, like "approved" or "free".

**How:** A circular stamp with bold text drops from 240% scale to about 92% and settles at 100% in 0.3s, tilted -14°, with a small screen shake on impact.

**Use when:** A stamp hits the screen, like "approved" or "free".

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

A big title, an underline drawing in, and a subtitle.

**How:** The title fades up (0.4s), an accent underline draws under it (0.4s), then the subtitle fades in (0.3s).

**Use when:** A big title, an underline drawing in, and a subtitle.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-lgo-191` — Chapter Title

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.6s*

A big number and title for each part of the video.

**How:** A large accent mono number (01, 02…) slides in, then the chapter title fades up beside or under it 0.15s later.

**Use when:** A big number and title for each part of the video.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

*workhorse · high · depth · evidence 0 · 0.6s*

A price or discount tag swings in.

**How:** A yellow tag-shaped label swings in from its hole side, from -90° to +12°, -6° and settles over 0.6s.

**Use when:** A price or discount tag swings in.

A bar fills with a percentage, like loading or progress.

Numbers 1, 2, 3 pop in with a connecting line.

### `al-lgo-196` — Quote Card

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.8s*

A quote or key line with its author.

**How:** A large accent quote mark scales in, then the quote text fades up line by line, then the author name fades in, each 0.2s apart.

### `al-lgo-197` — Stat Bars

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.6s · 0.1s stagger*

A bar chart grows in, for numbers and comparisons.

**How:** Vertical bars grow from the baseline to their values over 0.6s, each starting 0.1s after the previous one, with alternating brand colors.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

A ring fills to a percentage.

**Use when:** A ring fills to a percentage.

### `al-lgo-200` — Signature Write

Your signature writes itself at the end of the video.

**Use when:** Your signature writes itself at the end of the video.

## Per

### `al-per-201` — Text Behind Person

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 0.6s in*

A huge title behind your head with you in front, a top trend.

**How:** Place a very large bold title on a layer between the background and the person (use the person matte), so the head overlaps the letters. The title rises in with M-004 style.

**Use when:** A huge title behind your head with you in front, a top trend.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-per-202` — Color Pop

*workhorse · calm · depth · evidence 0 · 0.4s*

The background goes black and white while you stay in color.

**How:** Using the person matte, desaturate only the background to 0% and darken it slightly over 0.4s; the person keeps full color.

**Use when:** The background goes black and white while you stay in color.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-per-203` — Echo Trail

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · loop*

Transparent copies of you trail behind your movement.

**How:** Duplicate the person layer 2–4 times, each delayed by 3–5 frames and at decreasing opacity (30%, 15%…), so movement leaves an echo trail.

**Use when:** Transparent copies of you trail behind your movement.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-per-204` — Clone Trio

*workhorse · high · depth · evidence 0 · 0.3s per clone*

Multiple copies of you in the same shot.

**How:** Composite 2–3 mattes of the person from different takes side by side; each clone pops in (scale 90% to 100% with fade) 0.3s apart.

**Use when:** Multiple copies of you in the same shot.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-per-205` — Doodle Outline

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.8s draw*

Animated hand-drawn doodles around the person.

**How:** Draw loose white hand-drawn strokes (a crown, sparks, an outline arc) around the head that write on over 0.8s and wiggle slightly while held.

**Use when:** Animated hand-drawn doodles around the person.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-per-206` — Sticker Cutout

*workhorse · high · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.4s*

The person becomes a white-bordered sticker that pops.

**How:** Using the person matte, add a thick white outline (about 1% of the width) and a soft drop shadow, then pop the sticker in with a slight tilt (scale 0 to 108% to 100%).

**Use when:** The person becomes a white-bordered sticker that pops.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-per-207` — Pop-Out Frame

*workhorse · high · depth · evidence 0 · 0.5s*

The person breaks out of a frame, a 3D feel.

**How:** A rounded frame shows the background; the person matte is layered above it so the head sticks out over the top edge of the frame. The frame scales in first.

**Use when:** The person breaks out of a frame, a 3D feel.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-per-208` — Portrait Mode

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 0.5s*

A blurred background with the person sharp, like a phone portrait.

**How:** Using the person matte, blur only the background to about 1.5% over 0.5s while the person stays sharp.

**Use when:** A blurred background with the person sharp, like a phone portrait.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-per-209` — Silhouette Fill

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.3s*

The person turns into a solid brand-color silhouette, poster style.

**How:** Using the person matte, fill the person with a flat accent color (keep the matte edge soft) and fade it in over 0.3s on a beat.

**Use when:** The person turns into a solid brand-color silhouette, poster style.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-per-210` — Neon Outline

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · loop flicker*

A glowing neon edge traced around the person.

**How:** Trace the person matte edge with a 0.8% mint line plus a wide glow, and flicker it on like neon (see M-056).

**Use when:** A glowing neon edge traced around the person.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-per-211` — Spotlight Follow

*workhorse · calm · camera · evidence 0 · loop*

Everything goes dark except a light circle that follows you.

**How:** Darken the frame about 85% except a soft circle around the person; the circle tracks the head position every frame.

**Use when:** Everything goes dark except a light circle that follows you.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-per-212` — Halftone Person

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.4s*

The person rendered in halftone dots like old print.

**How:** Inside the person matte, overlay an accent halftone dot pattern (dot size tied to brightness) with a multiply blend.

**Use when:** The person rendered in halftone dots like old print.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-per-213` — Background Flash Swap

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · per beat*

The background color flips on every beat while you stay.

**How:** Using the person matte, replace the background with a solid color that changes on every beat (cycle 3–4 brand colors).

**Use when:** The background color flips on every beat while you stay.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

## Aud

### `al-aud-214` — Waveform

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · live*

A waveform that moves with your voice.

**How:** Analyze the voice track loudness (RMS) per frame and draw 30–60 thin rounded accent bars whose heights follow the audio around a center line.

**Use when:** A waveform that moves with your voice.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-aud-215` — Equalizer Bars

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · live*

Bars that bounce with the audio or music.

**How:** Split the audio spectrum into 6–10 frequency bands and draw a vertical gradient bar per band whose height follows that band with quick attack and slower release.

**Use when:** Bars that bounce with the audio or music.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-aud-216` — Circular Visualizer

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · live*

Audio bars arranged in a circle around your photo.

**How:** Place 24–48 accent bars radially around a circular avatar; each bar length follows one frequency band of the audio.

**Use when:** Audio bars arranged in a circle around your photo.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-aud-217` — Beat Flash

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · per beat · 0.15s*

A light flash on every beat of the music.

**How:** Detect beats in the music track; on each beat flash a white overlay to about 40–85% and fade it out over 0.15s.

**Use when:** A light flash on every beat of the music.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-aud-218` — Beat Zoom

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · per beat · 0.2s*

The frame pulses a zoom on every beat.

**How:** On each detected beat, jump the frame scale to 112% and ease back to 100% over about 0.2s.

**Use when:** The frame pulses a zoom on every beat.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-aud-219` — Beat Shake

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · per beat · 0.15s*

A short shake on every heavy beat.

**How:** On each strong beat (kick), shake the overscaled frame (106%) with 2–3 quick offsets of ±2% over 0.15s.

**Use when:** A short shake on every heavy beat.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-aud-220` — Audio Pulse Ring

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · live*

A ring around your photo that swells with your voice.

**How:** Draw an accent ring around a circular avatar; its scale (100–118%) and opacity follow the voice loudness each frame.

**Use when:** A ring around your photo that swells with your voice.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-aud-221` — Waveform Caption

*workhorse · calm · camera · evidence 0 · live*

A caption with a small live waveform under it.

**How:** Show the caption as usual and draw a compact waveform (M-214) just under it, following the voice.

**Use when:** A caption with a small live waveform under it.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-aud-222` — Mic Pulse

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · loop · 1.5s*

A microphone icon with ripples, for podcasts and voice.

**How:** A mic icon sits at the center while thin rings expand from it every 0.5s and fade (see M-150).

**Use when:** A microphone icon with ripples, for podcasts and voice.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-aud-223` — Podcast Card

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 0.5s in*

A podcast episode card with a photo and waveform.

**How:** A light card with avatar, episode title, show name and a small live waveform slides up with a spring and holds.

**Use when:** A podcast episode card with a photo and waveform.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-aud-224` — Volume Meter

*workhorse · calm · depth · evidence 0 · live*

A level meter rising and falling with the voice.

**How:** Stack 8–12 segments vertically; segments light up from the bottom with loudness (green, then yellow, then red at the top).

**Use when:** A level meter rising and falling with the voice.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-aud-225` — BPM Counter

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · per beat*

A BPM number with a dot pulsing on the beat.

**How:** Show the tempo as a mono number with "BPM" and a dot that flashes to 150% on every beat.

**Use when:** A BPM number with a dot pulsing on the beat.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

## Scr

### `al-scr-226` — App Window Pop

*workhorse · high · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.4s*

A desktop app window pops up while you explain.

**How:** A rounded window with three title-bar dots and a title scales from 60% to 104% to 100% with a fade over 0.4s, showing your screenshot or screen recording inside.

**Use when:** A desktop app window pops up while you explain.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-scr-227` — Phone Scroll

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 2s scroll*

Shows an app or page scrolling inside a phone.

**How:** A phone frame with rounded corners shows your screen recording or a long screenshot that scrolls up smoothly inside it, then eases to a stop.

**Use when:** Shows an app or page scrolling inside a phone.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-scr-228` — Laptop Mockup

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 0.6s in*

Places your screen recording inside a laptop.

**How:** A laptop mockup (screen bezel and base) rises 10% with a fade over 0.6s; your screen recording plays inside the screen area.

**Use when:** Places your screen recording inside a laptop.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-scr-229` — Browser Window

*workhorse · high · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.4s*

A website inside a browser window with a URL bar.

**How:** A browser window with dots, a URL bar showing your site, and the page content pops in; the URL can type itself first (see M-180).

**Use when:** A website inside a browser window with a URL bar.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-scr-230` — Phone Slide In

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.5s*

A phone with your app slides in next to you.

**How:** A phone mockup slides in from the side edge with a slight tilt that straightens over 0.5s, then holds beside the speaker.

**Use when:** A phone with your app slides in next to you.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-scr-231` — Cursor Click

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 1s*

A mouse cursor glides over and clicks a button.

**How:** A cursor arrow moves along a smooth curve to a button, scales to 85% on click, and a white ring expands from the click point.

**Use when:** A mouse cursor glides over and clicks a button.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-scr-232` — Zoom to Cursor

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.6s*

A zoom that follows the cursor in a screen recording.

**How:** In a screen recording, zoom to about 180% centered on the cursor position over 0.6s, follow it smoothly while zoomed, then zoom back out.

**Use when:** A zoom that follows the cursor in a screen recording.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-scr-233` — Modal Pop

*workhorse · high · depth · evidence 0 · 0.3s*

A dialog pops up over a dimmed background.

**How:** The background dims to about 55% black while a rounded dialog card scales from 90% to 102% to 100% over 0.3s.

**Use when:** A dialog pops up over a dimmed background.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-scr-234` — Toggle Switch

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.3s*

A switch flips from off to on.

**How:** A pill toggle: the knob slides to the other side over 0.3s while the track color changes from gray to the accent.

**Use when:** A switch flips from off to on.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-scr-235` — Loading Spinner

*workhorse · calm · depth · evidence 0 · loop · 0.8s*

A "one moment" spinner before the result.

**How:** A ring with one accent segment rotates one full turn every 0.8s; replace it with the result when it finishes.

**Use when:** A "one moment" spinner before the result.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-scr-236` — Notification Stack

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.3s each*

Notifications stacking up, like many messages arriving.

**How:** Notification cards drop in from the top one after another, 0.4s apart; each new card pushes the earlier ones down slightly.

**Use when:** Notifications stacking up, like many messages arriving.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-scr-237` — Keyboard Shortcut

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.6s*

Shows a shortcut like Ctrl + C being pressed.

**How:** Key caps appear side by side; each key presses down (moves 2% and turns accent) in order, 0.15s apart.

**Use when:** Shows a shortcut like Ctrl + C being pressed.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-scr-238` — Tab Switch

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.35s*

Tabs change and the content slides.

**How:** An accent underline slides from one tab to the next while the content panel slides across in the same direction over 0.35s.

**Use when:** Tabs change and the content slides.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-scr-239` — Form Fill

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · ~0.8s per field*

Form fields fill in one after another, for tutorials.

**How:** Each labelled field types its value in order (see M-082), and a checkmark appears at the end of each field when done.

**Use when:** Form fields fill in one after another, for tutorials.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-scr-240` — Upload Progress

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 1.2s*

A file uploading with a progress bar.

**How:** A file card with an icon and name shows a progress bar filling from 0 to 100% while the percentage counts up, then a check appears.

**Use when:** A file uploading with a progress bar.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

## Trk

### `al-trk-241` — Label Follow

*workhorse · any · camera · evidence 0 · live*

A label that sticks to a moving object.

**How:** Track a point on the object (optical flow or a tracker) and attach a label with a small pointer above it; the label follows the point every frame with slight smoothing.

**Use when:** A label that sticks to a moving object.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-trk-242` — Tracking Ring

*workhorse · any · sound · evidence 0 · live*

A ring that follows an object to point it out.

**How:** Track the object and draw a mint ring slightly larger than it, centered on the tracked point, with a soft pulse.

**Use when:** A ring that follows an object to point it out.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-trk-243` — Face Blur

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · live*

Hides a face or a plate for privacy.

**How:** Detect and track the face (or plate) and cover it with a rounded box that blurs what is behind it about 2.5%, following it every frame.

**Use when:** Hides a face or a plate for privacy.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-trk-244` — Callout Line

*workhorse · any · camera · evidence 0 · 0.6s*

A line draws from an object to a note beside it.

**How:** A thin line draws from the tracked point to a corner over 0.6s, then a small note box fades in at the end of the line.

**Use when:** A line draws from an object to a note beside it.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-trk-245` — Screen Replace

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · live*

Puts another image inside a phone screen in the video.

**How:** Track the four corners of the screen in the footage and warp your image or recording onto that quad every frame (corner pin), with a slight glare overlay.

**Use when:** Puts another image inside a phone screen in the video.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-trk-246` — Arrow Follow

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · live*

An arrow that keeps pointing at a moving thing.

**How:** Track the object and keep an accent arrow just above it pointing down, bobbing slightly while it follows.

**Use when:** An arrow that keeps pointing at a moving thing.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-trk-247` — Emoji Follow

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · live*

A sticker or emoji that follows a moving object.

**How:** Track the object and stick a sticker (or emoji image) on it, scaled to its size and following its position and rotation.

**Use when:** A sticker or emoji that follows a moving object.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-trk-248` — Path Trace

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · live*

Draws the path an object travelled.

**How:** Track the object and draw a dashed accent line along its past positions that builds up as it moves.

**Use when:** Draws the path an object travelled.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

## D3

### `al-d3-249` — 3D Spin Text

*workhorse · calm · depth · evidence 0 · loop · 3s*

A word spinning around its vertical axis in 3D.

**How:** Rotate the text around the Y axis with perspective, one full turn every 3s; keep the back face visible or mirrored.

**Use when:** A word spinning around its vertical axis in 3D.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-d3-250` — Extruded Text

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · loop · 4s*

Thick extruded text like a solid object.

**How:** Give the text a stacked, darker accent depth (6–10 offset layers) and gently tilt it in 3D (±14°) on a 4s loop.

**Use when:** Thick extruded text like a solid object.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-d3-251` — Parallax 2.5D

*workhorse · calm · depth · evidence 0 · loop · 4s*

A still photo moves in layers as if it has depth.

**How:** Separate the subject from the background (matte or depth map); move the background slowly one way and the subject the other way, with a 115% scale to hide edges.

**Use when:** A still photo moves in layers as if it has depth.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-d3-252` — Card Flip

*workhorse · any · depth · evidence 0 · 0.6s*

A card flips to reveal the answer.

**How:** A card rotates 180° around the Y axis with perspective over 0.6s, showing its back side with the reveal text.

**Use when:** A card flips to reveal the answer.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-d3-253` — Cube Spin

*workhorse · calm · depth · evidence 0 · loop · 4s*

A spinning 3D cube for a logo or product.

**How:** Build a cube from six faces with preserve-3d, tilt it -20° on X and rotate it a full turn on Y every 4s; put the logo on the faces.

**Use when:** A spinning 3D cube for a logo or product.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-d3-254` — Tilt Card

*workhorse · calm · timeline · evidence 0 · loop · 4s*

A card tilting as if held in your hand.

**How:** Tilt a card on X and Y (±12–16°) with perspective on a smooth 4s loop, with a soft shadow beneath it.

**Use when:** A card tilting as if held in your hand.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-d3-255` — Layer Explode

*workhorse · any · timeline · evidence 0 · 0.8s*

Design layers separate apart in 3D.

**Use when:** Design layers separate apart in 3D.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

*workhorse · calm · depth · evidence 0 · loop · 6s*

Cards rotating on a 3D ring to show several items.

**How:** Place 5–8 cards evenly around a 3D ring (rotateY steps + translateZ) and rotate the ring slowly.

**Use when:** Cards rotating on a 3D ring to show several items.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

### `al-d3-257` — Float Shadow

*workhorse · calm · depth · evidence 0 · loop · 3s*

**How:** Bob the object up 6% with a slight rotation while its drop shadow grows softer and lighter at the top of the motion.

**Use when:** A product or logo floats with a shadow that changes below it.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.

**Use when:** A coin tosses and flips, like heads or tails.

**Avoid when:** For static cards or when the scene is already busy with multiple elements.
